lines: A buyer has opened a PayPal dispute.
What the shop does next,
decides what it costs.
Answered while it's still a
dispute, it costs no PayPal fee.
Let it become a claim and lose,
and the fee is fourteen euros.
For a busy shop, twenty-eight.
Even when the shop wins.
And disputes cost more than fees:
a single customer-care contact, by phone,
chat or email, costs about eight dollars.
Every dollar lost to fraud costs a
merchant about four dollars sixty.
And big merchants give up on almost
half of their card chargebacks,
and win only one in five
of those they fight.
That's where Second Look comes in.
It's an AI that reads every PayPal
dispute and the evidence behind it,
runs the checks a specialist
would, and drafts the answer.
Nothing is sent until you approve it.
Meet Linen and Paper, a made-up shop
with about two thousand orders a month.
Marta answers customers, and can give
back up to thirty euros on her own.
Giulia manages the team.
Marta opens her helpdesk.
Dario has written.
Next to his email, Second Look shows
his PayPal dispute, already reviewed.
Its answer: defend with evidence.
She opens the case.
The courier recorded the apron as
delivered three days after it shipped,
to the address on Dario's PayPal account.
Dario has disputed four of his five
orders, and took two of them to a claim.
And what each way out costs: refunding
now, twenty-six euros out of pocket.
Defending costs nothing, unless
PayPal later sides with him.
She defends. No refund: the proof goes
to PayPal, the reply goes to Dario,
and the ticket records who sent it.
Second Look also says
when the buyer is right.
Pablo sent a shirt back, and
the refund never went out.
It's eighty-nine euros,
over Marta's limit.
So the case goes to Giulia,
and nothing is sent.
Giulia sees Marta's note and her
reply, and approves the refund.
Then the overview: what
the open cases could cost,
and how far the shop is from
PayPal's busy-shop line.
And it runs on PayPal.
This is PayPal's sandbox:
a one-person shop, a real dispute.
The reply went to the buyer, and the
tracking went to PayPal as proof.
The AI recommends. Limits written in
code have the last word. You approve.
Second Look. Sell without fear.
